```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal vulnerable Flask app for CVE-2026-78683 — Insecure Deserialization
Run: python target_app.py   (listens on :5000)
Then: python poc.py 127.0.0.1:5000

Replicates the nltk flaw: a "model file" is loaded through an unpickler.
PATCHED: deserialization now routes through a RestrictedUnpickler that
overrides find_class() and refuses to resolve any global (class/function),
so __reduce__ gadget chains can no longer execute code. Benign, data-only
models (dicts, lists, primitives) still rebuild correctly.
"""
import base64
import builtins
import io
import pickle

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)

# Secret the app should never disclose. It is returned ONLY after attacker
# code has executed during unpickling — i.e. only on successful RCE.
MARKER = "PWNED_nltk_502_a7f3c9"

# Name of the process-global flag that injected code flips to prove execution.
CANARY = "_nltk_deser_pwned"


class RestrictedUnpickler(pickle.Unpickler):
    """Unpickler that refuses to resolve arbitrary classes/functions.

    The vulnerability was that the default unpickler did not override
    find_class(), so any global — and therefore any __reduce__ gadget —
    could be resolved and invoked. By overriding find_class() to reject
    every global reference, no code-execution gadget can be reconstructed.
    Pure data models (built from pickle's primitive opcodes) never hit
    find_class() and continue to load normally.
    """

    def find_class(self, module, name):
        raise pickle.UnpicklingError(
            f"global '{module}.{name}' is forbidden during model loading"
        )


def restricted_loads(raw: bytes):
    """Safe replacement for pickle.loads() using the restricted unpickler."""
    return RestrictedUnpickler(io.BytesIO(raw)).load()


@app.route("/health", methods=["GET"])
def health():
    return jsonify({"status": "ok"})


@app.route("/load_model", methods=["POST"])
def load_model():
    data = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
    encoded = data.get("model", "")

    # Reset the execution canary before every load so results are per-request.
    setattr(builtins, CANARY, False)

    try:
        raw = base64.b64decode(encoded)
        # FIXED: restricted deserialization of caller-controlled bytes.
        # find_class() is overridden to forbid arbitrary class resolution,
        # so a __reduce__ gadget in the stream can no longer run code here.
        # A benign, data-only model just rebuilds its structure.
        obj = restricted_loads(raw)
    except Exception as e:
        return jsonify({"status": "error", "detail": str(e)}), 400

    if getattr(builtins, CANARY, False):
        # Extra action beyond decoding the model: attacker code executed.
        return jsonify({"status": "loaded", "note": MARKER})

    # Ordinary, non-malicious model: no marker is ever disclosed.
    return jsonify({"status": "loaded", "object_type": type(obj).__name__})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(port=5000, debug=False)
```
